newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FPHC, Sumitomo in estate tie-up.
newsitem.headline: FPHC, Sumitomo in estate tie-up.

text.p: First Philippine Holdings Corp said on Thursday it had signed a joint venture agreement with Sumitomo Corp to develop a 300-hectare industrial park in Batangas, south of Manila.
The total project cost "will eventually amount to $100 million after all the phases are developed and taken up by strategic customers", FPHC said in a statement.
An official at FPHC said the first of two phases of the project would be completed by 2001.
FPHC said large multinational companies engaged in high-technology manufacturing, light and pollution-free industries would be invited to locate at the park.
FPHC said the agreement was signed on November 4 by FPHC chairman Oscar Lopez and Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara.
The Philippine Export Zone Authority has approved the registration of the first 75-hectares of land as a special economic zone, FPHC added.

Beside the joint venture, FPHC said it also signed a general business cooperation agreement with Sumitomo to explore other business ventures. Earlier, FPHC forged an 800-million peso flexible printed circuit manufacturing venture with Sumitomo.
